newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand patrolled a tight range on Tuesday in trade marked by good volumes and balanced amounts of importer and exporter interest, dealers said.

In late trade, it was trading at 4.4990/5020 against the dollar -- its weakest level of the day -- after trading at a strongest level of 4.4920 bid in the morning session. Late Monday it was quoted at 4.4985/5015 against the dollar.

"It's been very quiet...stuck basically between 49 and the figure all day. There are some sizeable trades going through but on both sides...It's very hard to make money at the moment," a dealers said.
Dealers said more of the same was expected for the rest of the week as the market paused ahead of the relaxation of exchange controls next Tuesday.
Perceptions have been growing that the removal of controls on individuals next week is unlikely to have any sizeable impact on the rand, given the amount of reserves the Reserve Bank has amassed.
However, they said some local banks would remain long dollars as a guard against uncertainty.
Dealers said more of the same was expected on Wednesday and the rand was expected to hold a 4.49 to 4.51 range on the dollar for the rest of the week.
The local currency had a more volatile day against sterling, sinking to its weakest level in five months of 7.5206 rand from 7.4885/4980 overnight.
Dealers said the rand's losses against the British unit was a pure reflection of sterling's recent gains against the dollar.
Cable was last orbiting its five-month high of 1.6725 posted on Tuesday, trading at 1.6665/70.
Against the other crosses, the rand was last quoted at 25.4865/5257 yen from 25.6813/7206 yen on Monday and at 0.3827/3832 marks from 0.3828/3831 marks previously.
The bond market was equally subdued, as institutional nibbling at the higher levels and jobber profit-taking kept the R150 stock in a 15.60 to 15.54 percent range.
It was last quoted at 15.575 percent.
"There has been a bit of trade. Small selling out of London, a bit of institutional nibbling at the 14.58 level tucking into a few of the R150s, but its been a quiet one," a trader said.
Dealers said the market was in search of fresh direction after its downhill run from the 14.88 percent level last Wednesday.
That could come in the form of latest consumer inflation data which will be released at 0900 GMT on Wednesday, dealers said.
A Reuters consensus poll of economists forceast May CPI would show a year-on-year rise of 9.8 percent compared with 9.9 percent in April.
Barring any surprises in the data, dealers said bonds were likely to mimic the currency market and wait for events post-July 1 to unfold.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were unchanged at 16.00 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was slightly lower at between 15.55 and 15.40 percent from 15.60 to 15.40 percent on Monday.
The money market shortage rose to 5.544 billion rand on Monday from 5.389 billion rand on Saturday, the Reserve Bank said.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 227.24 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday after selling 142.07 million rand's worth on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on the bond market on Monday were pegged at 8.77 billion rand.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
